A volcano erupts in Ecuador, sending smoke and a fiery glow into the sky. Frederic Church traveled to South America to see volcanoes, mountains and jungles for himself. The glowing sky and smoking peak are spectacular. It's a dramatic painting of nature's power.
paintings.k: This volcano is erupting! Can you see the smoke and the glowing sky?

paintings.t: A Storm in the Rocky Mountains, Mt. Rosalie
paintings.why: A huge storm swirls over a mountain peak in Colorado, with a gleam of sunlight on a lake. Albert Bierstadt, a German-born American painter, traveled west in 1863 and painted the Rockies. He named the peak after the wife of a friend. It's a dramatic and thrilling mountain scene.

President Abraham Lincoln, with his tall, thin face and deep eyes, is painted in a calm pose. George Peter Alexander Healy, an American painter, painted Lincoln from life in 1860 and made later copies. The portrait shows the kindness and sadness in the face. It's an important image of one of America's most beloved presidents.

A flock of cranes flies across a wide sky over a marsh, in a soft, cold light. Józef Chełmoński, a Polish painter, was famous for painting birds and the Polish countryside. He loved wide landscapes and wild animals. It's a beautiful picture of migration.
paintings.k: Count the cranes flying across the sky. Which direction are they heading?

paintings.why: A fashionable Parisian woman in a colorful kimono sits among Japanese objects, a big fan and a screen. Alfred Stevens, a Belgian painter in Paris, painted the trend for all things Japanese in the 1870s. The painting is a fun look at a fashion craze. It's an elegant portrait.

Jesus speaks to a crowd that has gathered in a sunny Mediterranean town, with a woman at the center. Henryk Siemiradzki painted this in 1873 in his bright Roman style. The sunlight and architecture are very clear. It's an important Polish religious painting.

The great rose-red temple of Petra in Jordan is carved into a cliff, with tiny people at its base. Church traveled to the Middle East in 1868 and visited Petra, a hidden city in the desert that few Westerners had seen. The painting shows the huge carved building glowing at sunrise. It's an adventure picture from a far-off place.
paintings.k: This temple is carved into a cliff. Who looks tiny next to it?

paintings.why: A broad river in South America shines in golden light, with misty green jungle and distant mountains. Church painted the 'River of Light' from his sketches in Ecuador. The warm glow of the sky is amazing. It's a luminous view of a faraway land.

paintings.t: Jews Praying in the Synagogue on Yom Kippur
paintings.why: Worshippers stand and pray in a crowded synagogue on Yom Kippur, the holiest day of the Jewish year. Maurycy Gottlieb painted this near the end of his short life and included himself in the picture as one of the men standing among them. Each face is different and carefully painted. It's the most famous painting of Jewish prayer and a treasure in the Tel Aviv Museum of Art.

People in a Roman house listen to a reader as he recites the great Greek poet Homer, in a bright marble room with a view of the sea. Lawrence Alma-Tadema, a Dutch-born painter who lived in London, painted ancient life with every marble detail. The picture shows the love of stories that we still share. It's a beautiful scene of ancient culture.

A young woman in a white dress looks calmly out of the frame. Fernand Khnopff, a Belgian Symbolist painter, painted the portrait of Jeanne Kéfer, a young girl. He is known for his dreamy, mysterious style. The portrait is both elegant and strange.

A young girl in a dark dress stands in a doorway, painted with tiny dots of color. Théo van Rysselberghe, a Belgian painter, used the pointillist technique, which makes the light sparkle. The dots blend together when you step back. It's a lovely portrait of a child.

A young woman guides her flock of sheep home at the end of the day, in soft golden light. Pissarro loved to paint country people at their work, because he felt the same dignity as in the lives of city people. He used small dots and dashes of color to make the light shimmer. It's a gentle image of rural life.
l: Fred Jones Jr. Museum of Art

paintings.why: People relax on the sunny beach at Menton, on the French Riviera, with the blue sea and mountains. Charles Conder, an English-born painter who grew up in Australia, painted this when he was only 20. The bright light and fresh colors are charming. It's an early hit.

In the Finnish epic poem the Kalevala, the maiden Aino is pursued by the old hero Väinämöinen, in a three-part painting. Akseli Gallen-Kallela painted this triptych in 1891, inspired by Finland's national legends. The painting is full of Finnish forest and lake scenery. It is a key work of Finnish national art.

A woman in a rich purple dress sits at a piano, painted with bright strokes of color. Théo van Rysselberghe painted Maria Sèthe, who later became the wife of the Belgian architect Henry van de Velde. The picture glows with color and music. It's a charming portrait.
l: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp

paintings.why: A family gathers in a small wooden church for a baby's christening, with light falling through the windows. Harriet Backer painted the inside of the old church at Tanum, near Oslo, with a quiet, glowing light on the old wood. It's one of her best-known paintings and a favorite in Norway. It shows how she could make a sacred space feel warm.

A quiet, shaded pool is surrounded by tall trees, reflecting the sky. Isaac Levitan painted peaceful, thoughtful landscapes of the Russian countryside. His quiet mood and his soft colors became very influential. It's a calm, dreamy scene.

A couple embraces in front of a window, with the curtain and the dark shapes nearby. Edvard Munch painted several pictures of kisses, which were among his favorite subjects. The shapes of the two people almost melt together. It's a very personal and quiet moment.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: The Viking explorer Leif Erikson stands in the bow of a longship, gazing at the shore of a new land, with his crew behind him. Christian Krohg painted this in 1893 for the World's Columbian Exposition in Chicago, which celebrated Columbus. Norwegians wanted to remind everyone that Vikings reached North America around the year 1000. It's a proud picture of Viking history.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: A big crowd of businessmen in dark suits crowd the floor of the Copenhagen Stock Exchange. Krøyer painted a huge group picture with dozens of portraits. It's a clever, busy scene of the working world. It's a famous picture of Danish business life.

A man stands at a seashore while a woman with long hair seems to melt away, with her hair flowing in the wind. Edvard Munch painted about the pain of parting. The colors of sea and sky are quiet, but the mood is sad. It's one of his emotional pictures of love and loss.

A wide Paris boulevard in spring sunshine is lined with trees in new leaf and busy with walkers and horse-drawn carriages. Pissarro painted a whole series of this boulevard in different seasons and weather. This one is bright and fresh. Together they show how one place can change all year.

A Black sailor lies on the deck of a broken boat, surrounded by sharks, as a waterspout twists in the distance and a ship sails far away. Winslow Homer painted this in 1899, after traveling to the Caribbean. The painting makes people wonder whether he will be saved. It's one of his most famous and powerful works.

The hero Kullervo, in a rage, stands in a stormy landscape and curses his fate, in a scene from the Finnish Kalevala. Akseli Gallen-Kallela painted this dramatic picture in 1899. Kullervo is a tragic figure in the Finnish epic. It's a powerful painting from Finnish national romanticism.

Two farmers rest in a green field with their oxen while storks wander nearby. Józef Chełmoński, a Polish painter, was famous for painting birds and the Polish countryside. White storks come to Poland every summer and are loved as a symbol of good luck. It's a charming picture of country life.
paintings.k: Can you find the storks? What are the farmers doing?

paintings.why: Hundreds of people in formal clothes gather in a huge hall in Melbourne in 1901 as the first Parliament of Australia is opened. Tom Roberts spent years painting 269 portraits of the guests. The nickname 'The Big Picture' is well earned, as the canvas is huge. It's a record of the birth of a nation.

A big three-part painting shows a young pioneer couple in the Australian bush, with the husband swinging an axe, the wife listening to the sounds of the forest, and, in the last panel, a city rising where the forest was. Frederick McCubbin painted this in 1904 to celebrate the settlers. Today, we also ask what the Aboriginal people lost. It's one of Australia's most famous paintings.

A woman in a rose-pink gown sits in a quiet pose, painted with soft, warm color. Thomas Pollock Anshutz was a Philadelphia painter and teacher who taught many famous artists at the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts. He painted this late in his career. It's a delicate, gentle portrait.

The king Gustav Vasa rides into Stockholm in 1523 on a white horse, welcomed by crowds, when Sweden became independent from Denmark. Carl Larsson painted this huge mural in 1908 for the National Museum. Swedes celebrate this event as the founding of modern Sweden. It's an important national painting.

A woman irons clothes in a room full of color, painted in bold strokes. Rik Wouters, a Belgian artist, painted his wife Nel at everyday work in his home. The picture glows with bright, happy colors. It's one of the most beloved Belgian paintings.
l: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp

paintings.why: A dapper art dealer in a hat sits with a confident, slightly sly look. Paul Guillaume was one of the first people to sell Modigliani's art, and Modigliani painted him more than once. The portrait shows how an artist could turn a friend and supporter into a stylish, graceful shape. It hangs in a museum in Paris.

Modigliani painted his friend, the painter Moïse Kisling, who was also Jewish and came from Kraków in Poland. The two artists lived and worked near each other in Paris and helped each other through poor times. The picture shows Kisling in warm tones and Modigliani's long, simple lines. It's a portrait of friendship between two outsiders who became part of the Paris art world.

A rainy New York street is lined with flags, glistening with reflections. Childe Hassam painted a series of 'Flag Paintings' during World War I, when the flags were hung to support the American cause. The rain makes the colors shimmer on the pavement. It's a famous American Impressionist painting.

Modigliani is famous for portraits, but this rare landscape shows a small house and a tree in warm, simple colors. He painted it in 1919 in the south of France, where he went for his health. It is one of only a few landscapes he ever painted. It's a quiet glimpse of the artist outside his usual subjects.

Four little birds perch on a wire attached to a crank, and they seem to sing as the handle turns. Paul Klee painted this strange machine in 1922. It might be a joke about how machines can imitate nature, or a bit scary. It hangs in the Museum of Modern Art in New York, and kids often love it.
paintings.k: How many birds are on the wire? What do you think would happen if you turned the crank?

paintings.why: A round face made of circles, squares and triangles with big eyes and a pink-orange cheek. Paul Klee painted this in 1922, and the name 'Senecio' comes from a plant that means 'old man.' It looks like a clown or a mask. It's one of his most famous pictures.
paintings.k: This face is made of squares, circles and triangles. Can you name each shape you see?

paintings.why: Geometric shapes in gray, black and white are stacked into an abstract design that looks like a suit of armor. Ragnhild Keyser was a Norwegian painter, among the first women in Norway to study art abroad, and she explored modern styles. The picture is strong, simple and bold. It's an interesting piece of modern Norwegian art.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: Wild waves curl and crash in swirling gold and blue patterns on a folding screen, with white foam like tiny claws. Ogata Kōrin painted this in the early 1700s, and the waves look both realistic and like a design. Years later, Hokusai would paint his famous wave. It's one of the great sea pictures of Japan.
paintings.k: The waves have curved, claw-like shapes. What do they remind you of?

paintings.t: The Qianlong Emperor in Ceremonial Armor on Horseback
paintings.why: The Qianlong Emperor sits on a horse in shining armor, in a formal portrait. Giuseppe Castiglione painted the emperor in 1739, mixing Western realism with Chinese traditions. Qianlong ruled China for 60 years in the 1700s. It's a proud portrait of one of China's greatest emperors.

A huge scroll full of thousands of people, shops, boats and bridges shows a busy day in the city of Suzhou in the 1700s. Xu Yang, a court painter, spent years on it, painting every shop and sign in detail. You can spend hours finding little scenes of daily life. It's one of the most famous city scenes in Chinese art.

General George Washington stands tall in front of a cannon after the battle of Princeton, in 1777. Charles Willson Peale, a painter and a soldier himself, painted it from life. Washington stands with confidence. It's one of the most famous portraits of Washington as a leader.
l: Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts

paintings.why: A huge circular painting shows the whole view of the town of Thun in Switzerland and the surrounding Alps, as if you are standing in the middle. Marquard Wocher painted this panorama in 1814, and it is one of the oldest surviving panorama paintings in the world. People used to stand in a special building and turn around to see all of it. It's an early kind of virtual reality.

paintings.t: Episode of the September Days 1830, on the Grand Place of Brussels
paintings.why: Fighters in the Belgian Revolution of 1830 rush across the Grand Place in Brussels, flags flying, with a wounded man on the ground. Gustaaf Wappers painted the dramatic and patriotic scene five years after the revolution. It helped inspire Belgians as they built a new country. It's a big Romantic history painting.
l: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

paintings.why: An ancient Roman arch stands in ruins in a landscape in Italy, in the golden light of evening. Thomas Cole loved to paint the ruins of the ancient world. The quiet ruins remind us that great empires fade. It's a thoughtful, romantic landscape.

A man and his child walk by a grave, in a sad and quiet mood. Jozef Israëls was a Dutch painter of Jewish background, known as the leader of the Hague School. He painted poor families and fishermen with deep sympathy. It shows how art can show feelings of loss gently.

A group of Portuguese explorers and Indigenous people gather around a big cross at the first Catholic Mass held in Brazil in 1500. Victor Meirelles painted this in 1861 as a founding image of the nation. The Indigenous viewers are shown as curious bystanders. It's one of the best-known paintings in Brazil.

A black storm approaches over a calm bay as the sky grows dark and the water glows eerily. Martin Johnson Heade painted this in 1859, with a sense of drama right before the storm. A lone sailboat is the only sign of people. It's one of the most mysterious American paintings.

Giant granite peaks and a glowing lake spread out in the high Sierra Nevada, with mist and golden light. Bierstadt painted this to show how large the American West was. Crowds in the East paid to see his paintings. It's a perfect example of the grand scale of Western painting.

A snowy volcano rises above a lake and forest in Oregon, in the glow of late light. Albert Bierstadt painted the Pacific Northwest on his travels. The calm water reflects the mountain. It's a peaceful and majestic view.

Odin, the chief of the Norse gods, leads a ghostly army of riders across a stormy sky in the Wild Hunt. Peter Nicolai Arbo made several versions of this scene, based on Scandinavian folk tales. The flying horses, warriors and dogs are thrilling. It's the most famous painting of Norse myth.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design
paintings.k: Find the dogs running with Odin. Which one is the biggest?

paintings.why: Native Americans sit in a council in a meadow in California, with mountains rising behind them. Albert Bierstadt traveled in the American West and painted Indigenous people as part of the landscape. The painting shows a moment of gathering and discussion. It's a record of the West as one artist saw it.

paintings.t: Portrait of Professor Benjamin H. Rand
paintings.why: A man in a dark suit sits in a chair, with a serious face and a book. Thomas Eakins painted his friend, Professor Rand, a doctor and a teacher at Jefferson Medical College in Philadelphia. The dark colors and honest face show Eakins's realism. It's a thoughtful portrait of a scientist.
l: Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art

paintings.why: A woman sits near a window, reading in the soft light. Hans Heyerdahl was a Norwegian painter who painted quiet indoor scenes and portraits. The gentle light shows his skill. It's a peaceful moment at home.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.t: Free Period in the Amsterdam Orphanage
paintings.why: Girls in black and white dresses and caps rest and chat in the sunny courtyard of an orphanage in Amsterdam. Max Liebermann painted this when visiting the Netherlands, where he admired the work of Dutch masters. The play of light and shade through the trees is lovely. It's one of his best-known early works.

Fishermen push a boat into the sea from the beach at Skagen, in the bright light of the north. Oscar Björck, a Swedish painter, spent time with the artists' colony in Skagen. The scene shows real work by the shore. It's a lively picture of fishing life.

Workers burn wood into charcoal in the Australian bush, with the smoke and trees around them. Tom Roberts painted the lives of workers in the bush with great honesty. He was a leader of the Heidelberg School. It's a picture of a hard job.

A mother and her children sit around a sunny table for breakfast in a bright room. Hanna Hirsch-Pauli, a Swedish painter, painted this warm family scene in 1887. The glowing sunlight and morning mood are charming. It's one of the most famous paintings by a Swedish woman artist.
paintings.k: Look at the breakfast table. What do you like to eat in the morning?

paintings.why: A golden Australian landscape of dry grass, gum trees and a faraway blue range of hills, in the heat of summer. Arthur Streeton painted this in 1889 in Eaglemont, near Melbourne, with a group of artist friends. It is one of the most famous Australian paintings. The bright light made it a favorite.

Men in an Australian woolshed shear sheep, in a busy scene of work, with sunlight streaming through the roof. Tom Roberts painted this in 1890 and it is probably the most famous Australian painting. It shows the hard but proud life of the sheep farms. It's an icon of Australian life.
paintings.k: Look at the sunlight coming through the roof. What are the workers doing?

paintings.why: Two girls in warm winter clothes walk through a snowy street, looking out from under their hats. Isaac Israëls, a Dutch Impressionist, loved painting city people in motion. The quick brushwork makes the snow and the figures feel fresh. It's a charming winter moment.
paintings.k: What do you think the girls are doing in the snow?

paintings.why: A woman sits in a chair, looking a bit tired or sad, in a dim room. Thomas Eakins painted this quiet portrait, and the sitter's honest face is typical of his work. It hangs in the Phillips Collection in Washington. It's a famous portrait for its honesty.

paintings.t: I lock my door upon myself
paintings.why: A woman sits in a dark room with her face turned away, with a lyre and a closed door. The title comes from a poem by Christina Rossetti. Fernand Khnopff painted this in 1891, a mysterious picture about being alone with your thoughts. It's one of the most famous Belgian Symbolist paintings.

A fox runs across a deep snowy field while a flock of hungry crows swoops down to attack it. Winslow Homer painted this in 1893 at his home on the coast of Maine. The winter scene is both beautiful and harsh. It's one of the most dramatic animal paintings in American art.
l: Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts

paintings.why: A woman and a child tend a fire of brush in a field in Finland, with smoke curling up in the evening light. Eero Järnefelt painted this in 1893, showing traditional slash-and-burn farming. It is one of Finland's best-loved paintings. The glowing smoke and soft sky are lovely.

paintings.t: The Garden of the Amsterdam Orphanage
paintings.why: Girls in simple uniforms rest and walk in the shade of old trees, with spots of sunlight on the ground. Max Liebermann painted the orphanage garden many times, and each version is a study of light and shade. His loose brushwork is typical of his later Impressionist period. It's a peaceful, lovely scene.
l: Strasbourg Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art

paintings.why: Villagers in folk costumes dance outdoors on a summer evening in the Swedish region of Dalarna, with a golden light and music. Anders Zorn painted this in 1897, and it became one of Sweden's most loved paintings. Midsummer is the biggest holiday in Sweden. It's a happy picture of dancing under the northern sun.

Two women sit by a calm bay in the soft, pale light of a Nordic summer night, when the sun hardly sets. Richard Bergh, a Swedish painter, painted this in 1899 to capture the dreamy mood of the northern evening. The still water and the glowing sky are magical. It's one of the most beautiful Swedish landscapes.

A woman sits in front of a beautifully tiled prayer niche, in a mosque or a shrine, with a calm, thoughtful look. Osman Hamdi Bey painted the tiles in great detail, because he knew Ottoman art very well. The blue tiles are brilliant. It's a lovely picture of Ottoman art and architecture.

A group of writers and artists gather in a room to listen to the poet Émile Verhaeren read, in the soft light of a lamp. Théo van Rysselberghe painted this group portrait of his friends. Each face has its own personality. It's a picture of friendship and poetry.

The famous German philosopher Friedrich Nietzsche is painted in a strong, bold style. Edvard Munch made this portrait in 1906 for a Swedish collector, even though Nietzsche had died in 1900, so he painted him from a photograph and from memory. The expressive lines seem to show an intense thinker. It's a portrait of an idea as much as a man.

A woman in a gown sits in a room and prepares to go out, in a calm and elegant room. Edmund Tarbell was a Boston painter who made graceful pictures of women at home. The light and the quiet mood are lovely. It's a charming piece of American Impressionism.

Women in long, pale dresses sit and take tea in a sunlit room, in a soft and dreamy style. Richard Edward Miller was an American Impressionist who spent time in the art colony at Giverny, France, where Monet lived. The light is gentle and warm. It's a pretty, relaxed picture.

A crowded New York tenement street is full of kids, parents and laundry, in the dusty, bright light of summer. George Bellows painted the Lower East Side, a neighborhood full of immigrants, including many Jewish families. The crowded lives are painted with energy and warmth. It's a famous picture of the city's working-class life.
l: Los Angeles County Museum of Art

paintings.why: Modigliani painted his friend Chaïm Soutine, a Jewish painter from a poor village in present-day Belarus. Soutine's own wild, swirling pictures were very different from this calm, simplified portrait. They shared a studio district in Paris, and Modigliani looked after him. Together they show how two very different styles could grow side by side.

A twisted pine bends in a strong wind, with whitecaps on the lake and clouds streaming across a blue and gold sky. Tom Thomson painted this in the winter of 1916–17, and it is one of the most beloved paintings in Canada. He drowned mysteriously in a lake in 1917, shortly afterward, which made him a legend. The painting hangs in the Art Gallery of Ontario.
paintings.k: Feel the wind on the trees. Which way is it blowing?

paintings.why: A swamp full of strange plants, shapes and creatures in a dreamy, watery landscape. Paul Klee, a Swiss-German painter, painted the picture as a small, playful world made of lines and colors. His art feels like a fairy tale or a game. It's a fun picture to explore.
paintings.k: Look for strange plants and creatures hiding in this swamp. Which one would you like to meet?

paintings.why: A boxer is knocked out of the ring and thrown over the ropes into the crowd in a famous 1923 prizefight. George Bellows painted the dramatic moment in 1924 from memory. He loved sports, and painted several famous boxing scenes. It's one of the best-known American sports paintings.

Gustav III, the king of Sweden, is crowned in a grand ceremony in 1772, in the Storkyrkan church in Stockholm, with a crowd of nobles around him. Carl Gustaf Pilo began the large painting but died before it was finished. The picture shows a bright, glittering moment in history. It's an important picture of Swedish royalty.

paintings.t: A Seascape. The coast of the Island of Rügen in Evening Light
paintings.why: Waves roll along the coast of the German island of Rügen in the soft light of evening. Johan Christian Dahl, the father of Norwegian landscape painting, painted this early in his career. He painted the sea and the clouds with careful study. It's a peaceful seascape.

Workers building a huge barrel, with Mount Fuji tiny in the middle of the circle of the barrel. Hokusai made this clever woodblock print by framing the mountain inside the round barrel. It's a playful trick that shows his humor. It's one of the most charming prints in the series.

paintings.t: Shipwreck on the Coast of Norway
paintings.why: A ship is wrecked on the rocky coast of Norway in a storm, with waves crashing and people struggling to survive. Johan Christian Dahl painted this dramatic picture in 1832, which was a huge success. He captured the power of the sea and the clouds. It's one of the great Romantic seascapes.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: Farmers and families in traditional costumes gather for a prayer meeting in a simple farmhouse, with plain wooden walls. Adolph Tidemand painted this scene of a Hauge movement gathering, a popular Norwegian religious revival. It's famous for its honest look at Norwegian country life. The picture has become a symbol of Norwegian folk culture.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: A slender birch tree bends in the wind in a storm, with swirling clouds behind it. Johan Christian Dahl painted the same birch tree in many versions. The tree stands for strength against the wind. It's a symbol of Norwegian Romanticism.

Women in a simple farmhouse sit together plucking geese, with the feathers floating in the sunlight. Max Liebermann, a Jewish painter from Berlin, was just starting out when he painted this large picture of ordinary labor. Some critics were shocked by the plain subject. It launched his career as a painter of working people.

Two children play at the water's edge in a Dutch fishing village, wearing simple clothes. Jozef Israëls spent summers in the fishing village of Zandvoort and painted its people. The soft light on the sand and sea is lovely. It's a charming and moving image of childhood by the sea.
paintings.k: Two children play at the water's edge. What do you think they are looking at?

paintings.why: Brazilian soldiers charge across a field in a big and chaotic battle in the Paraguayan War in 1868. Pedro Américo painted this giant picture in 1877. It shows the heroism and the chaos of war. It's one of the largest paintings in Brazil.

Brazilian and Dutch forces fight in a bloody battle in 1649 in the hills near Recife, in a big and chaotic scene. Victor Meirelles painted the battle of Guararapes in 1879. The picture became a symbol for the first national feeling in Brazil. It's an important battle in its history.

paintings.t: The Twelve-Year-Old Jesus in the Temple
paintings.why: A boy Jesus speaks with scholars in a temple, with a look of calm. Max Liebermann painted Jesus as a Jewish boy among Jewish teachers, which was shocking to some people in 1879 who wanted him portrayed in a more traditional way. The painting caused a big controversy in Germany. It shows how Liebermann challenged expectations from the start.

paintings.t: Portrait of a Wounded KNIL Soldier
paintings.why: A wounded soldier of the Dutch colonial army sits quietly with bandages. Isaac Israëls was a Dutch painter from a Jewish family, and the son of the famous painter Jozef Israëls. He painted this early in his career. It shows his interest in real people, even in sad moments.

A street in Tehran, with a few walls and trees in the afternoon sun. Kamal-ol-Molk was a leading Iranian painter who studied European techniques and painted scenes of everyday life in Persia. The detailed realism is typical of his style. It's a window into 19th-century Iran.

Immigrants on a ship's deck look out at their new home in Australia, as the ship sails into the harbor. Tom Roberts painted this scene of arrival in 1886 after he had made the voyage himself. The excited faces are very expressive. It's a famous picture about the hopes of new settlers.

A horse and rider gallop wildly to turn a stampeding flock of sheep away from a waterhole, in a dust cloud. Tom Roberts painted this in 1891 and the tension is amazing. It shows the dangers of work in the outback. It's a thrilling picture.
paintings.k: The horse and rider are galloping fast. Can you find the sheep?

paintings.why: Soldiers gather in a square in Rio de Janeiro on November 15, 1889, as Brazil becomes a republic and ends its monarchy. Benedito Calixto, a Brazilian painter, painted the scene a few years later. The celebration was peaceful. It's an image of an important turning point.

A group of bushrangers, outlaws, hold up a stagecoach on a dusty Australian road. Tom Roberts painted this in 1895 based on a real story he'd heard. The mix of danger and adventure was very popular. It's an exciting scene from Australia's wild past.
l: Art Gallery of New South Wales

paintings.t: Love at the Fountain of Life
paintings.why: A young couple and an angel stand among rocks and trees by a spring of water, in a dreamy, symbolic picture. Giovanni Segantini, an Italian painter who lived in the Alps, painted many pictures about life and nature. The fountain of life stands for the beginning of love. It's a quiet, thoughtful picture.

A wide plain of golden wheat and pale blue shadows stretches out under a huge purple-blue sky on a hot day. Arthur Streeton painted this in 1896, and its title is from a poem by Shelley. He captured the heat and bright light of an Australian summer. It's one of Australia's most loved landscapes.

A grand palace hall with walls of mirrors and a glittering ceiling, where a man in robes sits in the middle. Kamal-ol-Molk painted this masterpiece of the Golestan Palace in Tehran in 1896. The mirrors and glass reflect light in a dazzling way. It's his most famous painting.

paintings.t: Old man in front of children's graves
paintings.why: An old man stands in a graveyard, with children's graves nearby, in a sad and quiet scene. Osman Hamdi Bey painted this in 1903, and it's a strong picture of grief. The simple garden and tombstones are painted with great care. It's one of his best-known pictures.

A Jewish wedding is celebrated by a crowd in a village, with the bride and groom under a canopy. Jozef Israëls was born in a Jewish family in the Netherlands and sometimes painted scenes of Jewish life in later years. The picture is full of lively faces and warm light. It's a joyful record of a tradition.

A twisted pine tree stands alone on a rocky shore, with a glowing lake and a sunset sky behind it. Tom Thomson painted this in 1916, and it became one of the most famous paintings in Canada. The lonely tree stands for strength in the wild northern land. It hangs in the National Gallery of Canada in Ottawa.
paintings.k: Look at the tree's shape. Why do you think it grows like this?

paintings.why: Soldiers from Australia and New Zealand climb up a steep cliff under fire at Gallipoli, Turkey, in April 1915, a terrible campaign in World War I. George Lambert, an Australian war artist, painted this big picture after visiting the site. Each year, Anzac Day on April 25 honors these soldiers. It's a solemn and important picture for Australians.

A pale ghost woman with long black hair, in a white robe, floats in the air with no feet. Maruyama Ōkyo, a Japanese painter from Kyoto, is said to have started the style of painting ghosts without legs. Japanese ghost stories are very popular, and this ghost is one of the most famous. It's a spooky and beautiful image.
l: Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive
paintings.k: Ghost stories are popular in Japan. What is missing from this ghost?

paintings.t: Ayusi Sweeping Bandits with a Lance
paintings.why: A brave warrior, Ayusi, charges with a lance in a battle scene. Giuseppe Castiglione painted this to honor a hero of Emperor Qianlong's military campaigns in the 1750s. The dashing horse and rider are very lively. It's a great action picture from imperial China.

paintings.t: Flowering Plants of Summer and Autumn
paintings.why: Wildflowers and grasses sway in the wind on a pair of silver screens, with morning glories and bush clover. Sakai Hōitsu, a painter from Edo (Tokyo), wanted to continue the style of Ogata Kōrin. He painted the plants in soft colors. It's a lovely picture of the changing seasons.

A country house stands in the countryside near Oslo, with trees and a path. Johan Christian Dahl painted Frogner Manor when he visited Norway. The estate is now a park and a museum in the middle of Oslo. It's a picture of a place that has changed a great deal.

Blue and white morning glories climb up and fill the screen with green vines, in a bright, modern-looking design. Suzuki Kiitsu, a Japanese painter from Edo, was a student of Sakai Hōitsu. The flowers seem to float in the air. It's a graceful picture of a summer flower.

A mountain farm lies on a high plateau in Norway, with rocks and a stormy sky. Johan Christian Dahl visited Filefjell in his travels. The wild beauty of the mountains made him famous. It's a view of the rugged heart of Norway.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.t: Mountain Streams in Summer and Autumn
paintings.why: Rushing streams run through mountains, with trees in the bright greens of summer and the reds of autumn. Suzuki Kiitsu painted the seasons on a pair of screens. The curving water adds a flowing rhythm. It's a lovely way to see time pass in one picture.

An elderly woman sits by a fire, resting in a plain room, with a quiet, tired face. Jozef Israëls loved to paint simple people with great dignity. The title comes from a Dutch saying about growing old. It's a thoughtful look at old age.

A richly decorated Ottoman room, with a low table, rugs and a few people in colorful robes. Osman Hamdi Bey was a leading Ottoman painter and also the founder of Turkey's first archaeological museum. He painted objects and patterns with the same care he gave to his scientific work. It's a window into a Turkish home.

A young girl in a long dress sits and reads from the Qur'an, in a quiet and peaceful scene. Osman Hamdi Bey painted this in the 1880s. The soft light and her calm face are gentle. It's a tender picture of faith and learning in Istanbul.

Villagers carry a coffin through a snowy countryside, with mourners following in a long line. Erik Werenskiold, a Norwegian painter, painted this to show real Norwegian farm life without prettiness. It was celebrated as one of the first truly Norwegian paintings. It's a serious, moving picture.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: An elegant woman in a long dress sits calmly, in the rich colors of an Ottoman room. Osman Hamdi Bey studied painting in Paris, and he brought European skills back to Istanbul. The detail of the fabric and tiles is lovely. It's a graceful portrait.

Women spread linen to bleach in the sunshine across a meadow in the Netherlands. Max Liebermann loved the quiet beauty of country work, which he studied during long stays in Holland. The wide landscape and bright light are very peaceful. It's a classic of German-Dutch realism.

The men who wrote Norway's constitution in 1814 gather in a hall at Eidsvoll, in a big group scene. Oscar Wergeland painted this to commemorate the founding of modern Norway, which Norwegians celebrate every year on May 17. It shows the 112 delegates at work. It's a very important painting for Norwegians.

A long line of poor people stand in the cold outside a charity office, waiting for help in the snow. Christian Krohg painted this in 1889 to draw attention to poverty in Kristiania (Oslo). He wanted his art to make people care. It's one of the most important Norwegian paintings about social issues.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.t: A meeting in the Royal Danish Academy of Sciences and Letters
paintings.why: Dozens of serious men in dark suits sit and stand around a large table at a meeting. Krøyer painted this as a huge group portrait for the Royal Danish Academy of Sciences. It shows many leading scientists of the time. It's a record of Denmark's great minds.

Hunters walk through the dunes of Skagen with their dogs, in the clear light of the north. Krøyer painted the artists and locals of Skagen in the open air. The sandy shore and sky are bright. It's a lively picture of life by the sea.

Jesus is shown to the crowd by Pontius Pilate in a bright, dramatic scene in Jerusalem. Antonio Ciseri, a Swiss-Italian painter, painted this famous work with great realism. It is a very well-known picture in Italy. It's a dramatic Bible scene.

A woman in the elegant clothes of the 8th-century Tempyō era of Japan, painted in a Western oil style. Fujishima Takeji was a Japanese painter who studied in Europe and brought back new ideas. The painting mixes Japan's ancient past with a modern style. It's a famous picture from Meiji-era Japan.

A river runs through the northern Ontario wilderness, with dark evergreens and a sky glowing orange and pink at sunset. Tom Thomson painted this in 1915, and it is one of his most famous pictures. It was bought by the Canadian government and hangs in the National Gallery of Canada. It's a classic image of the Canadian north.

People whirl on a fairground carousel in a blaze of bold, swirling color, painted as if everything is spinning at once. Mark Gertler, a British painter whose Jewish parents came from Poland, made this during World War I, as a bitter picture of people being swept around by forces they can't stop. The harsh colors and rounded shapes make it unforgettable. It's regarded as his masterpiece.

Pale blue ice melts on a lake in spring, with dark trees and a golden sky. Tom Thomson painted the thawing lake in Algonquin Park. The painting is an early sign of spring in the north. It's one of his finest winter-to-spring scenes.

A woman sits in front of a large bunch of sunflowers, in a bright, sunny style. Isaac Israëls painted many women in colorful dresses and loved flowers. The yellow sunflowers glow behind her. It's a joyful portrait.

A small white church stands in the dark forest of Yuquot on Vancouver Island, with a glowing light around it. Emily Carr painted it in her bold, expressive style, and its glowing, simple shape makes it unforgettable. Also called 'Church at Yuquot Village', it shows her gift for combining nature and faith. It's one of the most famous Canadian paintings and hangs in the Art Gallery of Ontario.

A round, cheerful monk with a big belly and a bag, Hotei, is painted with a few quick, playful strokes. Hotei is a happy god of good luck in Japanese and Chinese tradition. Ogata Kōrin drew him with simple lines and a lot of humor. It's a friendly picture that makes people smile.
paintings.k: Hotei is a happy god. What is he carrying?

paintings.why: Eight horses of different colors stand and pose in a calm landscape. Giuseppe Castiglione, known in China as Lang Shining, painted the emperor's favorite horses. His lifelike style, with shadows and shapes, was new for Chinese painting. It's a handsome picture of the emperor's stable.

A few sprigs of ivy turn red and gold in autumn, painted in a few quick strokes with a fresh, flowing style. Ogata Kenzan was a famous potter and painter in Kyoto and the younger brother of the painter Ogata Kōrin. He painted and decorated pottery with seasonal plants. It's a quiet picture that celebrates the beauty of the passing season.

Puppies play under a trellis of morning glories in the soft light of dawn. Maruyama Ōkyo was famous for painting animals from life, which was new in Japan, and his puppies are a famous example. The soft fluffy dogs have made many people smile. It's an adorable picture from the 1700s.
paintings.k: Count the puppies and see how each one is doing something different. Which is the sleepiest?

paintings.why: A huge white elephant on one folding screen and a giant whale on the other face each other across the two sides, like a big playful puzzle. Itō Jakuchū painted them in 1795 in a dotted, quirky style that looks like a pixel picture. The two giants, one of land and one of sea, seem to say hello. It's a fun, funny masterpiece of Japanese art.
paintings.k: The elephant and the whale are made of tiny squares. Which one do you think is bigger?

paintings.t: Quisisana seen from a Terrace with the Royal Household
paintings.why: A view of a palace on the Bay of Naples is seen from a terrace, with the royal family's household nearby. Johan Christian Dahl visited Italy in 1820 and painted the sunny coast. The warm light and blue sea were a great change from his northern home. It's a bright, sunlit travel picture.

A castle near Dresden, Germany, sits on the bank of the Elbe River in the light of dawn. Johan Christian Dahl, a Norwegian who settled in Dresden, painted the castle in a clear, calm style. His friend Caspar David Friedrich lived in the same city. It's a peaceful scene of the Elbe valley.

paintings.t: Two Men before a Waterfall at Sunset
paintings.why: Two men stand before a roaring waterfall in the glow of a red sunset. Johan Christian Dahl was famous for waterfalls and mountains, which he painted in a dramatic Romantic way. The tiny figures show the power of nature. It's a classic of Norwegian Romanticism.

A prehistoric stone burial monument stands in a snowy field in Denmark, under a winter sky. Johan Christian Dahl painted these ancient stones, which were fascinating to Romantic artists. The old stones seem to guard a secret. It's a mysterious winter scene.

paintings.t: Actor Arashi Rikan II as Osome
paintings.why: A kabuki actor plays the role of a young woman in a colorful woodblock print. Ryūsai Shigeharu was a printmaker in Osaka who made pictures of famous kabuki actors, which fans collected. The actor's pose and costume show the drama of the theater. It's a snapshot of the stage in old Japan.

Jewish figures sit and stand by a riverbank, hanging their harps in the trees, in a scene based on a Bible psalm about mourning for Jerusalem during exile in Babylon. Eduard Bendemann, a German painter of Jewish background, painted it in 1832, when he was 21. It was a huge success and made him famous. It's one of the best-known Jewish subjects in 19th-century German painting.

Two young girls in simple dresses gather water at a well in a calm landscape. Eduard Bendemann was a German painter from a Jewish family in Berlin who became a respected professor in Düsseldorf. He painted both Bible scenes and everyday life with soft, polished detail. It's a gentle, charming country scene.

A great glacier shines in the Swiss Alps, between steep mountains, with tiny people and houses in the valley. Thomas Fearnley, a Norwegian painter, traveled across Europe and painted famous landscapes. He was friends with Johan Christian Dahl and with the English painter Turner. It's a vast Alpine view.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: The city of Dresden shines in the silver light of the moon, with its domes and towers by the river. Johan Christian Dahl lived in Dresden for most of his life. He painted the moonlight with great beauty. It's a magical night view of an old city.

paintings.t: Scene in the Northwest: Portrait of John Henry Lefroy
paintings.why: A British officer and scientist, John Henry Lefroy, stands in a winter landscape in the Canadian northwest, dressed in a warm fur coat, with sled dogs. Paul Kane met him on his trip across Canada. Lefroy was studying the earth's magnetism. It's a famous Canadian portrait of the fur trade era.

Ships sail in the harbor of Copenhagen under a glowing moon, with the city behind them. Johan Christian Dahl was a student in Copenhagen before he went to Dresden. The moonlight shimmers on the water. It's a beautiful night harbor scene.

A saint stands in a kitchen holding a pot, in a simple and colorful scene. San Pascual Bailón is the patron saint of cooks in Mexico, and he is shown among pots and kitchenware. Agustín Arrieta was famous for kitchens and still lifes. It's a charming picture of Mexican faith and food.

Fishermen carry one of their own in from the shore, with the wind and the waves behind them. Jozef Israëls was inspired by the harsh lives of fishing families in the Netherlands. The picture is sorrowful and powerful. It reminds us of the danger of life at sea.

A woman warrior on a winged horse flies through a stormy sky, as a Valkyrie from Norse myth. Peter Nicolai Arbo was a Norwegian painter who illustrated the sagas and Norse mythology. His dramatic pictures helped give Norway a picture of its Viking past. It's an exciting scene from the old stories.

A woman in a dress holds a wilted flower, with a sad, thoughtful look. Manuel Ocaranza was a Mexican painter who died young, at 31. The dead flower stands for lost love or the shortness of life. It's a famous romantic painting from Mexico.

A close portrait of a weary, noble-looking man with a faraway gaze: the legendary Wandering Jew, a man condemned to roam forever. Maurycy Gottlieb painted Ahasuerus with dignity instead of horror, giving a sad folk legend a feeling of grandeur. It shows how Jewish artists reworked old stories. It's a powerful, quiet portrait.

paintings.t: The Mancorbo Canal in the Picos de Europa
paintings.why: A steep, rocky gorge with a rushing river rises between the high peaks of the Picos de Europa in northern Spain, with a stormy sky. Carlos de Haes, a Spanish painter born in Belgium, helped introduce realistic landscape painting to Spain. He made this picture of the mountains after a visit in 1876. It's a famous landscape of northern Spain.

The great Valley of Mexico spreads out beneath a huge sky, with volcanoes, lakes and small villages. José María Velasco is the most famous Mexican landscape painter, and he painted this in 1877. He was also a scientist who studied plants and animals. It's a grand and loving portrait of his country.
A young woman sits and braids her long hair, lost in thought. Christian Krohg painted private, quiet moments with a Realist eye. The soft light and calm are charming. It's a peaceful scene.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: People gather in a dark house at night for a wake, in a quiet, sad scene. José María Jara, a Mexican painter, painted this in 1889. It shows the customs of mourning in Mexico. It's a moving picture of community.

A large crowd gathers in a field in Quebec in 1837 for a famous political meeting. It was an important event in the Rebellion of 1837 in Lower Canada. Charles Alexander Smith painted it decades later to remember the struggle. It's a snapshot of Canadian history.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.why: A calm Buddhist figure, Guanyin, stands on a roaring dragon above clouds and waves. Harada Naojirō was a Japanese artist who studied in Germany and painted in the Western style. The painting mixes ancient Asian subjects with modern oil painting. It's a striking meeting of East and West.
l: The National Museum of Modern Art

paintings.why: A young girl in a long dress leans over to study a flower, in a sunlit garden. Paul Peel painted children with great charm. The picture won him a medal at the Paris Salon. It's one of Canada's best-known paintings of childhood.
paintings.k: The girl is studying a flower. What would you ask her about it?

paintings.why: A family sits together at home after a church ceremony, in their best clothes. Carl Frithjof Smith, a Norwegian painter who lived in Germany, painted quiet scenes of family life. The mood is peaceful and warm. It's a gentle picture of a special day.

A calm Norwegian summer evening, with a soft glow in the sky and the stillness of the land. Halfdan Egedius was a young Norwegian painter who died at only 25, but who painted with great sensitivity. The quiet mood is almost like music. It's a gentle and dreamy landscape.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.t: Hattery Mars on the Nieuwendijk in Amsterdam
paintings.why: A hat shop on a busy Amsterdam street, with the window full of hats and the crowd walking past. Isaac Israëls painted the lively life of Amsterdam, which made him a leading painter of the city. The scene is quick and bright. It's a snapshot of 1890s shopping.

paintings.t: Two maids on the Lijjnbaansgracht in Amsterdam
paintings.why: Two maids stand and chat by a canal in Amsterdam, with brick houses and water behind. Isaac Israëls painted ordinary women and children in the city's streets. The bold, loose style is typical of the Amsterdam Impressionists. It's a lively scene of everyday work and conversation.

People pause on the street to look at a shop window, with their reflections in the glass. Isaac Israëls loved scenes of city life, with its crowds and shops. The quick brushwork gives a sense of moving life. It's a modern city picture from the 1890s.

A woman in a light dress sits in a sunny garden among the flowers. Krøyer painted his wife Marie in the summer light in Skagen. The bright sunlight and soft pastel colors are happy. It's a loving portrait of his wife.

A weary figure walks across a landscape strewn with the bones of others, past burning cities and fleeing people. Samuel Hirszenberg, a Jewish painter from Łódź in Poland, painted this huge picture as a sad vision of the history of persecution. It's a dramatic and sorrowful image. It hangs in the Israel Museum.

paintings.t: Portrait of the Painter Lovis Corinth
paintings.why: A sturdy man with a stern, serious look sits at his easel, painted in strong dark strokes. Lovis Corinth was a fellow German artist and Liebermann's colleague, though they often disagreed. Liebermann, a leader of the Berlin Secession, painted many portraits of colleagues. It's a fair look at a great painter.

A young woman with a dark hat, painted with confident, loose strokes. Isaac Israëls was known for lively portraits of friends and city people. The style is fresh, fast and modern. It captures her personality in a few strokes.

A garden with a country house shines in the sun with bright colors, with leafy trees and flowers. Max Liebermann painted the gardens he visited in the Netherlands, which he loved for the brilliance of the light. The picture is bright and happy. It's a good example of his late Impressionist style.

paintings.t: The Terrace at the Hotel Louis C. Jacob in Nienstedten on the Elbe
paintings.why: Guests relax at tables on a shady terrace overlooking the Elbe River, with the sun speckling through trees. Max Liebermann painted this scene in the hotel that is still there in Hamburg today. The light and the leisurely mood are lovely. It's a gem of German Impressionism.

A crowd of weary people trudge in a long line across a snowy plain, carrying children and belongings. Samuel Hirszenberg painted the suffering of Jewish families forced from their homes, based on the real events of his time. It's a powerful picture of a hard chapter of history. It reminds us of the resilience of people.

paintings.t: Alegoría del trabajo y Alegoría de la construcción
paintings.why: Two panels show workers building and creating, in a bold, simple style. Saturnino Herrán was a Mexican painter who wanted to celebrate Mexico's own people and history instead of copying European art. He died young, at 31, in 1918. His works helped inspire the great muralists who came after him.

A woman holds a candle and a small offering in a quiet church or chapel, with a golden glow. Ángel Zárraga, a Mexican painter who lived in Paris, painted this in 1912, blending Mexican themes with European modern styles. The soft light and strong shapes make a peaceful scene. It's a thoughtful picture of faith.

An Indigenous couple in a boat of marigolds in the canals of Xochimilco, carrying flowers for the Day of the Dead. Saturnino Herrán painted 'La ofrenda' in 1913, and it is one of the best-known paintings about Mexican traditions. The bright orange cempasúchil flowers guide the spirits home. It's a loving picture of how Mexicans remember their families.

A thoughtful man in traditional Iranian dress looks out in a realistic portrait. Kamal-ol-Molk painted a number of portraits of Iranians in the early 1900s. The detail in the face and clothing is careful. It's a good example of Iranian realism.
l: Islamic Consultative Assembly Museum of Iran

paintings.why: A kitchen glows with blue walls, a table and sunlight pouring in. Ludvig Karsten was a Norwegian painter who liked strong colors and bold shapes. He lived a free artist's life and painted with a loose, vivid touch. It's a bright, modern look at an ordinary room.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: A woman from the Isthmus of Tehuantepec in southern Mexico wears the beautiful, embroidered dress and headdress of her region. Saturnino Herrán celebrated Mexican folk culture in his paintings. The Tehuana dress later became famous because Frida Kahlo wore it. It's a colorful portrait of Mexican heritage.

A girl in a white dress with long red hair looks calmly out of the picture. Eilif Peterssen painted many portraits of leading Norwegians and their families. This one comes from late in his career. It's a gentle, graceful portrait.

paintings.t: Two models, Epi and Gertie, in the Amsterdam Fashion House Hirsch
paintings.why: Two fashion models in elegant dresses at a fashion house in Amsterdam, painted with quick, confident strokes. Isaac Israëls was fascinated by modern fashion and city life. He painted this when he was in his fifties. It's a stylish picture of the Jazz Age.

The German poet Goethe, in a dressing gown, reads a book in a room full of women in an imagined Ottoman harem. Abdülmecid II painted this in 1918, and he was the last caliph of the Ottoman family and also a talented painter. It shows how Ottoman artists were interested in European culture. It's a very unusual meeting of East and West.

A woman in a robe stands in a swirl of orange-red flames, her hair and clothing streaming behind her. Uemura Shōen, one of Japan's greatest women painters, painted this in 1918, based on a legend of jealousy from a Noh play. The flames seem to come from her own feelings. It's a powerful picture by a master artist.

A man in a dark jacket with a long face sits against a swirly background, painted with thick brushstrokes. Soutine painted this portrait in the early 1920s, before he became famous. The strong colors and lively shapes show how he used paint to express feeling. It's a typical example of his unique style.

A fluffy tabby cat looks out at us with bright green eyes, sitting calmly with its fur painted in very fine lines. Takeuchi Seihō was a master painter from Kyoto who loved animals. The picture became a cultural treasure of Japan. It is one of the most famous cat paintings in the world.
paintings.k: Look at the cat's fur. The artist painted each tiny hair! What is the cat looking at?

paintings.why: Officials in wigs and robes gather around a big table in the early government of New France. Charles Huot painted this huge scene of Canadian history, which hangs in the Quebec legislature. It shows how the French colony of Canada was governed in the 1600s. It's a grand history painting.

A waiter in a white uniform stands stiff and serious with his arms at his sides. Soutine painted many hotel workers in Paris, with bold white uniforms in swirling paint. The unusual style makes the plain subject seem important. It's a well-known late portrait.

Gods and goddesses from Japanese legend stand in a misty sky above the sea, creating the islands of Japan with a jeweled spear. Kawamura Kiyoo painted this in a Western oil style, showing the old Shinto myth of the creation of Japan. The story says the god Izanagi and the goddess Izanami stirred the sea with a spear. It's a major painting from Japan's Meiji era.

paintings.t: Portrait of the Kangxi Emperor in Informal Dress Holding a Brush
paintings.why: The Kangxi Emperor sits in a relaxed pose, holding a brush, in a plain robe. The emperor ruled China for 61 years, longer than anyone else, and he painted and wrote poetry as well. This portrait shows him as a scholar, not only a ruler. It's a thoughtful picture of an emperor.

A first sketch for the famous painting of one hundred horses, with horses resting, swimming and playing in a landscape. Giuseppe Castiglione was an Italian missionary and painter who became the court painter of the Chinese emperors. He combined Western realism with Chinese painting. It's a rare look at how he planned a masterpiece.

Sparrows cling to a bending stalk of autumn millet, painted with great care for every feather and seed. Itō Jakuchū was an eccentric Japanese painter in Kyoto who owned a vegetable shop and raised chickens to study them. He is now celebrated as one of Japan's greatest painters of animals. It's a delightful close-up of nature.
paintings.k: How many sparrows can you find? Are any of them hiding?

paintings.t: The Qianlong Emperor's Southern Inspection Tour, Scroll Six: Entering Suzhou along the Grand Canal
paintings.why: A long scroll painting shows the Qianlong Emperor's procession as it travels along a canal, with boats and crowds. Xu Yang was one of the court painters who recorded the tour in a series of giant scrolls. Each scroll is full of details of the landscape and the people. It's a grand record of an imperial journey.

paintings.t: The Qianlong Emperor's Southern Inspection Tour, Scroll Four: The Confluence of the Huai and Yellow Rivers
paintings.why: Another scroll from the series shows the emperor's travels through towns and countryside, with tiny people and boats on the river. Xu Yang painted twelve scrolls about the Qianlong Emperor's tour of southern China. They are among the largest and most detailed pictures from the Qing court. It's a fascinating look at life in 18th-century China.

paintings.t: Moses with the Tablets of the Law
paintings.why: Moses holds the stone tablets of the Ten Commandments, with a calm and strong face. Moritz Daniel Oppenheim, often called the first Jewish painter of modern Germany, painted this early in his career. It was a way of showing Jewish heritage with pride in a time when Jews had few rights. It's an important early work by a pioneer.

paintings.t: A Cloud and Landscape Study by Moonlight
paintings.why: A study of clouds and a landscape in the pale light of the moon. Johan Christian Dahl was among the first painters to study clouds closely, like scientists. He painted them outdoors in quick studies. It's a lovely early example of looking at the sky.
l: Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco

paintings.t: Marriage Portrait of Charlotte de Rothschild
paintings.why: A young bride in a rich wedding gown is shown in a loving portrait. Moritz Daniel Oppenheim was a favorite painter of the Rothschild family, the famous Jewish banking family. He painted it with great care for rich fabrics and jewelry. It's a window into the elegant world of 19th-century Jewish high society.

A group of people gather around a young Shakespeare as he reads aloud a play. Solomon Hart was an English painter and the first Jewish member of the Royal Academy. He painted scenes from history and literature in great detail. It's a warm tribute to the power of storytelling.

paintings.t: Family of General Don Felipe Codallos
paintings.why: A Mexican general, his wife and children pose together in their finest clothes in a formal portrait. Agustín Arrieta was a painter from Puebla, Mexico, who painted portraits and scenes of everyday life. The details of the clothes and furniture are careful. It's a glimpse of Mexican society in 1838.

A young man with an earnest face looks out of the frame. Adolph Tidemand, a Norwegian painter who lived in Düsseldorf, Germany, painted portraits as well as scenes of Norwegian farm life. He helped create the image of Norway's peasants as national heroes. It's an early portrait from his career.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: A study of a horse in strong, lively lines. Adolph Tidemand made drawings and paintings of animals as practice for his big pictures of Norwegian life. The horse is full of character. It's a lovely small study.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.t: Milton Visiting Galileo when a Prisoner of the Inquisition
paintings.why: The English poet John Milton visits the aging Italian astronomer Galileo, who is held under house arrest by the Inquisition. Solomon Hart, the first Jewish member of the Royal Academy, painted this scene of two great minds meeting. It celebrates the courage of thinking freely. It's a moving image.

A young woman looks thoughtfully out of the canvas in a quiet, warm portrait. Lida Bendemann was the artist's own relative, painted with careful detail. Eduard Bendemann was a leading German painter. It is a tender portrait of a family member.

paintings.t: Actor Ichikawa Shiko as Kato Yomoshichi
paintings.why: A kabuki actor in a bold costume strikes a dramatic pose in a woodblock print. Konishi Hirosada was a printmaker in Osaka who made prints of famous actors. Fans collected such prints like trading cards. It's a picture of a Japanese theater star.

A lighthouse shines through a night sky on a rough coast, with waves and dark clouds. Peder Balke painted dramatic seascapes of northern Norway in quick, bold strokes. He was little known in his lifetime, but today he is seen as a brilliant artist. It's a moody and powerful picture.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.t: Landscape. Motif from the Numme Valley in Norway
paintings.why: A green valley in the Norwegian mountains, with a river, trees and a farm. Joachim Frich was a Norwegian painter who painted the romantic landscapes of his homeland. He studied in Germany and painted this valley in the 1850s. It's a typical early view of the Norwegian countryside.

Another version of Tidemand's scene of a farmhouse prayer gathering, with a dim room, simple clothing and serious faces. Tidemand painted several versions because the first was so popular. The soft light on the faces and the quiet atmosphere are moving. It's a picture of faith in Norwegian rural life.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.t: Zacharie Vincent et son fils Cyprien
paintings.why: Zacharie Vincent, a Huron-Wendat artist, painted himself and his son, dressed in traditional clothing. He is considered the first Indigenous painter in Quebec, and he signed his work 'the last of the Hurons.' It is a proud self-portrait that shows both identity and strength. It's an important work in Canadian art history.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.t: Lavater and Lessing Visit Moses Mendelssohn
paintings.why: A group of men gather in a study for a friendly but serious debate, with the Jewish philosopher Moses Mendelssohn at the center. Oppenheim painted a famous meeting between Mendelssohn and two Christian thinkers, a story about respect and tolerance. It was an important message for German Jews in the 1800s. It's a famous image in Jewish history.
l: Magnes Collection of Jewish Art and Life

paintings.why: The young shepherd boy Giotto draws a sheep in the dirt as the great painter Cimabue watches in amazement. According to legend, Cimabue saw Giotto's talent and took him as a student. José María Obregón, a Mexican painter, painted this famous story in 1857. It's about discovering a gift.

A young woman lies in the grass above the sea, lost in daydreams. Jozef Israëls, a Dutch painter of Jewish background, was the leader of the Hague School and often painted quiet, thoughtful moments. The soft light and dreamy pose invite you to wonder what she is thinking. It's a gentle picture of imagination.

paintings.t: The Return of the Bear Hunter
paintings.why: A hunter returns home with a bear he's killed, as the family and villagers greet him. Adolph Tidemand painted scenes of Norwegian rural life that were popular across Europe. The hunter is a hero. It's a scene from a harsh but proud way of life.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: Big waves crash under a sky of dark clouds in a moody, simple seascape. Peder Balke painted the rough seas of the north with a few strong brushstrokes. His art was forgotten for years, then rediscovered. It's a very modern-looking painting for 1862.

The artist Guadalupe Carpio paints herself with her family, in a warm group portrait. She was one of the first Mexican women to study at the Academy of San Carlos in Mexico City. The picture shows her family around her. It's an unusual self-portrait.

A general with a beard and a serious look stands in uniform. Ulysses S. Grant led the Union army in the American Civil War and later became the 18th president of the United States. This portrait was painted by Ole Peter Hansen Balling, a Norwegian-born painter who fought in the Civil War himself. It's a link between Norway and American history.

A Jewish family rests on the Sabbath in a warm home, with candles and a quiet mood. Moritz Daniel Oppenheim became famous for a series of paintings showing traditional Jewish family life. Many of his pictures were turned into prints and hung in homes across Europe. It's a loving look at a day of rest.

A woman greets her father at the door in a warm, joyful family scene. Maurycy Gottlieb, a Jewish painter from Galicia, studied under the great Polish painter Jan Matejko. He painted this when he was only in his early twenties; he died at 22, but left behind a few remarkable paintings.

A ship finds shelter from a storm at a safe harbor on the Norwegian coast, with a sky of clouds. Hans Gude, a leading Norwegian painter, was a master of ships and the sea. He taught many younger painters in Germany. It's a dramatic coast picture.

Gottlieb, a young Jewish painter, dresses himself as a Polish nobleman, wearing a fur-trimmed coat and a fur hat. He painted this when he was about 20 as a way of saying that Jews were also a part of Polish culture. The proud pose and rich costume are meant to be a statement. It's one of the best-known self-portraits in Polish-Jewish art.
l: Museum of the History of Polish Jews

paintings.why: Jesus speaks to a crowd in Capernaum, with Jewish listeners gathered around him. Maurycy Gottlieb, a Jewish painter, imagined Jesus as a Jewish teacher in a Jewish town. He painted it in the last year of his life. It shows how a Jewish artist could look at a Gospel story as part of his own culture.

Mountains rise over a calm fjord, with the water reflecting the sky and a few boats. Hans Gude painted the grand scenery of Norway, which made him one of the most famous Norwegian painters. The picture shows the beauty of the fjords. It's a classic Norwegian view.

A woman sits alone in a dim room, with her head bowed. Jozef Israëls was a master of painting the loneliness of poor, working people. The few colors and soft light create a deep mood. It's a moving painting from the Hague School.

A cobbler sits and works at his bench in a small shop, surrounded by shoes and tools. Max Liebermann was fascinated by workers and their daily tasks. The warm, gloomy light and the careful composition show his respect for the craft. It's a quiet picture of a simple trade.

The 21st president of the United States, Chester A. Arthur, sits for a formal portrait with a calm, serious expression. Ole Peter Hansen Balling was a Norwegian-born painter who moved to America and painted famous Americans. His portraits tell us how both countries are connected. It's an interesting piece of Norwegian-American art.

A woman sits in a Paris room, with the soft light from a window. Kitty Kielland was one of the first women to become a leading Norwegian landscape painter, and she lived in Paris for a time. This interior shows her skill with light. It's a quiet room scene.

paintings.t: Portrait of the Swedish Painter Karl Nordström
paintings.why: A man with a strong, thoughtful face looks out of a dark background. Christian Krohg, a Norwegian painter, painted his friend Karl Nordström, a Swedish artist. The two met in the artists' colony in Grez-sur-Loing near Paris. It's a portrait of friendship between Nordic artists.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.t: Breakfast I. The Artist's Mother and Brother
paintings.why: A mother and son sit at a simple breakfast table in a warm, bright room. Gustav Wentzel painted this scene of his own family, in a very honest and everyday way. Many Norwegian painters of the 1880s wanted to show real life as it was. It's a cozy and truthful picture.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: A woman sits in a dim room, with deep blue shadows and soft, warm light. Harriet Backer was one of Norway's most important painters, and was famous for painting the glow of light inside a room. She taught many younger artists. It's one of the most beautiful pictures of indoor light in Norwegian art.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: A mother tenderly holds her baby close in a quiet room. Christian Krohg, a Norwegian painter and writer, often painted mothers and the lives of ordinary women. The soft light shows the love between them. It's a gentle, warm picture.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: Families sit at tables under chestnut trees in a Bavarian beer garden, with sunlight shimmering through the leaves. Max Liebermann painted this in Munich and later became the leading German Impressionist. He liked to paint people enjoying leisure. It's a cheerful scene of German life.

Orphan girls sit and walk together in a leafy garden, in the dappled sunshine. This is another version of the orphanage garden theme Max Liebermann loved. He painted it again and again in different lights. It shows his love for the way the light moves through leaves.

A calm Norwegian summer night, with the sun low in a sky of pink and blue and a quiet lake. Kitty Lange Kielland painted the northern light in the midnight summer, when it never gets fully dark. The picture captures a sense of peace. It's a famous Norwegian landscape.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: A small stream runs through a snowy landscape, with the blue and white of winter. Frits Thaulow was a Norwegian painter who loved to paint water, in rivers and streams, often in winter. He painted with a pure and clear touch. It's a lovely view of a Norwegian winter.

A woman looks out with a calm, direct gaze in a warm, simple style. Christian Krohg painted his models and friends honestly, in the Realist tradition. He was a leading painter in Norway's art world. It's a lively portrait.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: A thoughtful man looks out of the picture. Krøyer painted the English painter Adrian Stokes, a friend he met in Skagen. The picture is a lively, quick sketch. It shows Krøyer's talent for capturing a person's character.

A woman sits in a room lit by a glowing paper lantern, with soft colors. Oda Krohg, a Norwegian painter and a leading figure in the Kristiania bohemians, painted this in 1886. Japanese objects were very fashionable in the 1880s. It's a lovely and modern picture.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: Two people sing or play music together in a quiet and cozy room. Peder Severin Krøyer painted scenes of music and friends in Skagen. The warm lamp light is lovely. It's a charming picture.

People wait quietly in a courthouse hall, looking tired and worried. Isidor Kaufmann was a Hungarian Jewish artist who painted Jewish life in Eastern Europe with warmth. This early work shows his talent for painting real people in everyday places. It reminds us how artists record everyday life.

A shoemaker works at his bench in a small farmhouse room, lit by a window. Harriet Backer was one of Norway's greatest painters, famous for the glow of light indoors. She studied in Munich and Paris and later taught many younger artists. The warm light and simple furnishings make an ordinary scene feel special.

A quiet blue night scene with the moon and shimmering water, with few figures. Eilif Peterssen was a Norwegian painter who liked painting history, portraits and mood. Many Norwegian painters in the 1880s painted this kind of atmospheric night. It's a calm and dreamy picture.

paintings.t: Portrait of the Painter Oda Krohg, b. Lasson
paintings.why: A woman in a red blouse stands confidently with her hands on her hips. Oda Krohg was a painter herself and Christian Krohg's wife, and an important figure in the Kristiania art world. Her husband painted her several times. It's a lively tribute from one artist to another.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: A large public square in Tehran with people going about their day. Kamal-ol-Molk, the court painter of Iran, painted what he saw with a European realism that was new in Persia. It's an important record of what the city looked like. It's a historical snapshot.

A family sits in a dark house, with a single lamp lighting their faces. Jozef Israëls painted the calm and warmth of simple lives in Dutch homes. The glow of the lamp is gentle. It's a cozy, quiet scene.

A ghostly hunter and his dog lead a pack of spectral figures across a snowy field in a haunting night scene. William Blair Bruce, a Canadian painter from Hamilton, Ontario, painted this in France. It tells an old folk tale about a ghostly hunt. It's a dramatic, spooky picture.

A quiet fjord scene with calm water and mountains in the background. Gunnar Berg was a Norwegian painter who painted the landscapes of northern Norway. The calm water is like a mirror. It's a peaceful picture.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: The Bible story in which Abraham is told to offer up his son Isaac, but an angel stops him at the last moment. Yosef Zvi Geiger was an artist born in Jerusalem during the Ottoman era. He painted it in a straightforward, heartfelt way. It's a rare early painting by an artist born in the Holy Land.
A young barefoot girl stands in a sunlit field with her sheep. Paul Peel painted country children in soft light. The peaceful scene was popular in Paris. It's a sweet pastoral picture.

A snowy landscape lit by a pink and gold evening sky, with blue shadows on the snow. Fredrik Borgen was a Norwegian painter who painted the quiet moods of winter. The painting makes the cold feel gentle and calm. It's a beautiful winter view.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: A young girl in a fur-trimmed coat and cap looks calmly out of the picture. Erik Werenskiold painted his family and close friends with honesty. He was one of the most respected Norwegian painters and also illustrated Norwegian fairy tales. It's an affectionate family portrait.

A folding fan painted with little portraits of artist friends. Asta Nørregaard, one of Norway's first professional women painters, worked in Kristiania (now Oslo) and was a supporter of other artists. A fan like this was a playful gift to remember friends. It's an unusual and charming piece of art.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: A young shepherdess stands in a sunny field in France with her sheep. Suzor-Coté, a Quebec painter, studied in Paris and loved the French countryside. He later painted Canadian winter landscapes. It's an early, gentle picture from his time in France.

Dancers in colorful costume and masks perform the ancient court dance called bugaku, as musicians play. Kanō Eigaku painted the scene in a classic Japanese style with fine details. Bugaku has been performed in Japan for over a thousand years. It's a lively picture of traditional performance.

A group of professors in black robes sit around a table, discussing business, in a group portrait. Max Liebermann was asked to paint the University of Hamburg's professors, and he gave each one a lively, individual look. It shows his gift for capturing character. It's a notable German group portrait.

Visitors stroll and play on the sunny beach at Scheveningen, the seaside resort near The Hague, under a wide sky. Isaac Israëls painted the busy beach with light, quick strokes. The tiny figures and sparkling sand are very lively. It's a happy summer day by the North Sea.

A woman sits at a table in a modern room beside a window with a view of the sea. Léon Bakst was a Jewish artist from Russia, best known for designing amazing costumes and sets for the Ballets Russes in Paris. His sense of color and mood made even simple scenes feel like a stage. This early work shows his stylish touch.

Samuel de Champlain steps off a boat at Quebec in 1608 as he founds the city, while the shoreline is shown behind him. Henri Beau, a Canadian painter, painted this to mark the 300th birthday of Quebec City. It's a scene from the founding of New France. It shows how Canadians remembered their history.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.why: A crowded dance hall in Montmartre in Paris, full of dancing couples and bright lights. Isaac Israëls painted this famous dance garden, which was also painted by Renoir and Van Gogh. His version is quick and full of motion. It's a lively picture of Parisian nightlife.

paintings.t: An Allegorical Wedding- Sketch for a carpet dedicated to Mr. and Mrs. David Wolffsohn Triptych (from...
paintings.why: A colorful design for a carpet, with symbolic figures celebrating a marriage. Ephraim Moses Lilien was a Jewish artist from Galicia, then part of Austria, who designed books, posters and carpets.
